html:
Ingombe Ilede is an archaeological site on a hill near the Zambezi river in southern Zambia, where rich burials of about the 15th century were found in 1960.

The dead were buried with gold beads, copper bangles, cross-shaped copper ingots used as money, iron tools, cotton cloth and glass beads from the Indian Ocean. They show that people on the middle Zambezi traded copper and ivory down the river to the Swahili ports on the coast.

The site belongs to the same world as Great Zimbabwe, whose rulers controlled the gold trade to the south. It is one of the clearest signs of wealth and long distance trade in Zambia before Europeans.
sum: Ingombe Ilede is an archaeological site on a hill near the Zambezi river in southern Zambia, where rich burials of about the 15th century were found in 1960.
